newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi Cola PR says income was overstated.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi Cola PR says income was overstated.

text.p: Pepsi-Cola Puerto Rico Bottling Co on Wednesday restated its results for the first and second quarter of fiscal 1996, saying that previous results overstated operating income and understated expenses.
The company said restated figures include a net loss of $0.03 per share, or $0.6 million, for the first quarter, rather than the $2.8 million net reported previously.
For the second quarter the restated figure is a net loss of $0.16 per share, or $3.4 million, as opposed to the previously reported net income of $2.3 million, the company said.

The company said its restated net sales figures are $29.4 million for the first quarter, rather than the previously reported $31.0 million, and $25.1 million for the second quarter rather than $26.9 million.
The company attributed the mistake to accounting irregularities that resulted in understated discounting and marketing expenses and overstated operating income.
The company said additionally that its board had named a new chairman, John Beck, who has been a company director since 1987.
